say.text: Shirkuh was made vizier of Egypt, and given the titles al-Malik al-Mansur and Commander of the Troops. The caliph al-Adid received him politely, and arrayed him in the robe of the vizierate.

From that time Shirkuh held supreme authority, and he entrusted the general management of affairs to Salah ad-Din, on account of his great abilities and the knowledge, good judgment and administrative talents he showed.
A week ago I was a stranger with an army and a debt. Today I have a title, a palace and a treasury I cannot count. I trust the first more.
The army is hungry, uncle. And the treasury is less than they say.
That is your department now. Count it, and tell me what is left. I will do what I am good at: sit and be a vizier where they can see me.
